claims.evidence: 'what': reversibility testing 'supports an asthma diagnosis but does not settle it'. NG245 (via summary): no single test has high enough sensitivity and specificity to be diagnostic in all cases; reversibility sensitivity modest. Population studies show similar reversibility in asthma and COPD, so the old 'helps separate asthma from COPD' was weak and the edit is right.

NG115 (via search): diagnosis suspected on symptoms and signs and supported by spirometry; post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.7 is the NICE threshold; older people with ratio <0.7 but no typical symptoms: consider alternatives; younger people with symptoms: consider COPD even if ratio >0.7. 'With typical symptoms, confirms airflow obstruction' is a fair paraphrase.
GOLD 2023 executive summary and later reports: spirometric criterion remains post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.7.

ERS/ATS 2022 standard: 5th and 95th percentiles of healthy population, z-scores -1.645/+1.645, used for LLN. 'Many laboratories report it' is supported by a UK ICB guideline noting ARTP uses LLN (not an authoritative host, but modest claim).

NG245: diagnose asthma when FEV1 rises by 12% or more and 200 mL or more from pre-bronchodilator (final wording 'or more'); NG245 also lists an alternative of 10% or more of predicted normal FEV1, and in adults the pathway places eosinophils/FeNO before reversibility. Draft says 'supports asthma', which is a softer, safe wording.
ERS/ATS 2022: significant bronchodilator response = change in FEV1 or FVC of more than 10% of the predicted value.

'A similar response is also seen in some people with COPD': population study (PubMed 31221806) found reversibility (>=12% and 200 mL) in 17.3% of asthma and 18.4% of COPD participants; GINA acknowledges reversibility is common in COPD.

whyOrdered: NICE QS10 / NG115: spirometry in people over 35 with a risk factor (generally smoking or a history of smoking) and one or more COPD symptoms (exertional breathlessness, chronic cough, regular sputum, wheeze).
Interpretation row 'Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.7': NICE severity table uses post-bronchodilator FEV1 as % predicted; diagnosis needs typical symptoms plus spirometry.

Record 1 value/unit/jurisdiction (FEV1/FVC below 0.7, post-bronchodilator, UK, NG115). Source URL is the guidance overview; better to point at https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng115/chapter/recommendations, section label 'Diagnosing COPD' is reasonable.
Record 1 context ends 'a ratio near the limit is repeated'. No retrieved NICE text says this (the retrieved caveat is about older people without typical symptoms and younger people above 0.7).
claims.newSentence: With typical symptoms, confirms airflow obstruction in COPD; older people with a ratio below 0.7 but no typical symptoms are considered for other diagnoses

claims.evidence: Record 2 (GOLD): fixed post-bronchodilator 0.7. GOLD 2023 executive summary (title returned from publications.ersnet.org/content/erj/61/4/2300239): fixed ratio may under-diagnose young adults and over-diagnose the elderly, especially mild disease, compared with LLN. Source URL, title and section 'Diagnosis' fine.

Record 3 (ERS/ATS): 5th/95th percentiles at z = -1.645/+1.645. 'same age, sex and height' is textbook-level standard wording about reference equations (GLI) not seen verbatim; harmless. Section 'Obstruction' unverified but reasonable.

Record 4 (NG245 12% and 200 mL, adults): final guideline wording 'FEV1 increase of 12% or more and 200 mL or more'. 'Not specific, also seen in some people with COPD' supported by NG245 limitations and PubMed 31221806. Suggest URL https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng245/chapter/recommendations; section label could be the NG245 recommendations heading on objective tests for diagnosing asthma in adults (not verified verbatim).

Record 5 (ERS/ATS BDR): 'more than 10% of predicted' FEV1 or FVC. Context 'Replaces the 2005 12% and 200 mL criterion in the ERS/ATS standard' is fair for ERS/ATS, but retrieved text says GINA and GOLD still use the 2005 criterion, so 'in the ERS/ATS standard' must stay.

Record 6 (over 35): NICE NG115 and QS10: over 35 with a risk factor (smoking/ex-smoking) and symptoms such as exertional breathlessness, chronic cough, regular sputum, wheeze (also frequent winter bronchitis). Context matches.

notes: Only one claim is unsupported: record 1 context 'a ratio near the limit is repeated'. NG245 gives an alternative adult criterion of 10% or more of predicted FEV1 which the draft does not mention; optional addition. NG115 recommendation on older people without typical symptoms was seen only through search summaries.
